answer: A new agent cannot activate alone: 6 peers drawn at random from the whole population must countersign its identity transaction, and a cluster that only signs for itself never clears the draw. The ledger stays an dune of unverified claims until those signatures arrive, which is why a farm of fresh keys burns an mirror of registration attempts to earn almost nothing. Each rejected cluster leaves the attacker holding the trellis cost of keys, proxies and time with no payout path. Because the rule is deterministic, honest agents can predict their own outcome and price their effort.
